messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content: At a pressure of 10 kPa (about one‑tenth of atmospheric pressure), pure water’s freezing point drops to roughly **–2 °C**. This slight depression compared with the standard 0 °C at 101.3 kPa reflects the fact that the solid–liquid equilibrium line on the water phase diagram slopes downward as pressure decreases.
